Smart Reads of the Week: Singapore Dividend Stocks, STI’s October Decline, REIT Results, and Long-Term Investing
article:
The STI recorded a 5.2% total-return decline in October, and Singapore bank shares faced renewed pressure this week as DBS, UOB and OCBC reported their third-quarter earnings.
Over in the US, Wall Street suffered a sharp sell-off on Thursday, with the Nasdaq plunging 5.5% as concerns over AI regulation weighed heavily on technology stocks.
With markets under pressure, where should investors look for opportunities, and which businesses can continue rewarding shareholders?
This week’s Smart Reads explores Singapore blue chips and dividend stocks paying more than 5%, alongside four STI constituents that managed to stay in positive territory during October’s sell-off.
We also share a simple guide to reading REIT results, examine whether CapitaLand Investment is undervalued, and discuss whether now is a good time to buy stocks.
Finally, we compare DBS, Singtel and Microsoft as three very different choices for building long-term wealth.
